messages:
alex: Heads up — we started seeing a latency regression on the nightly perf job after the FlashAttention merge (commit abc123). p50/p95 fine but p99 jumped ~2.3x for long-seq runs. Attaching quick profile snippet.

alex: PERF SNAPSHOT (seq=2048, batch=8):
```
throughput: 820 tokens/s -> 610 tokens/s
p50: 38ms -> 40ms
p95: 112ms -> 118ms
p99: 270ms -> 620ms
GPU util: 78% -> 92% (more stalling)
NVTX: long stall in attention_kv_loop
```

alex: Repro command I used: `./bench/run_inference.sh --model redwood-7b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --profile --kernels flash_fused`

maria: ugh. which upstream repo+commit? flash-attn main or our fork? and did the nightly switch kernel variants automatically?

alex: upstream flash-attn commit abc123 (merged yesterday). Our runtime picked `flash_fused` by default for that model; when I forced `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=paged` the p99 dropped back to ~300ms but throughput also down. So looks like fused variant has unexpected KV/cache behavior at long seqs.

sam: I can try a bisect. quick question — did the batching heuristics change recently? We had that heuristic tweak to prefer larger microbatches at seq>1024 last week. Could be interacting.

jordan: also flagging that vLLM merged a change to `kv_cache_prefetch` default two days ago (https://github.com/vllm/vllm/pull/987). That patch increases prefetch concurrency which can increase GPU memory pressure and change scheduling. Might amplify stall behavior in fused kernels.

lee: deploy-bot shows merge: `deploy-bot: merged flash-attn@abc123 -> main` at 1975012300.

sam: I'll run bisect across these axes: flash-attn commit range + our batching heuristic toggle + vLLM prefetch flag. Will post minimal repro matrix. ETA 2h.

maria: Good. Also try reproducing on a dedicated instance (no multi-tenant noise) and capture `nvprof`/`nsys` timeline for the attention kernel — want to see where threads block.

alex: attached a short `nsys` screenshot in thread (shows kernel serialization when kv cache flush happens). Behavior looks like synced memcpy/locks inside fused path.

jordan: if fused path is serializing NVLink transfers differently, xFormers changes could also matter; any vendor driver updates in the last 48h?

lee: infra: no driver roll in last 72h on the perf pool. Vendor provided a small patch to their cuops lib but we haven't rolled it to perf.

alex: immediate mitigation option: force kernel selection to `paged` for redwood-7b long-seq profiles via feature flag until we have root cause. Patch idea: add config override per-model: `runtime.model_kernels.redwood-7b = [paged, flash_fallback]`.

maria: agreed — do the flag and run longer soak on dedicated. Also open upstream issue in flash-attn with attached `nsys` trace and our minimal repro.

jordan: I'll prepare a minimal repro docker image that pins flash-attn@abc122..abc124 and vllm main/with/without prefetch flag so we can iterate reproducibly.

sam: progress update (1h): bisect narrowed to flash-attn commit abc120..abc123; abc121 introduces a change to the KV handling loop that looks suspicious. Running a microbench now.

alex: thanks. creating the feature-flag PR to pin kernel preference, will link in thread when ready.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch `runtime/kernel-prefs/redwood-7b` — tests: perf-smoke, integration, canary.

lee: action items: sam=bisect & repro; maria=soak + open upstream issue; jordan=image + vLLM combo tests; alex=feature-flag PR. Update here when you have results. :thumbsup:
